title: Bozo language - Wikipedia
text: In Nigeria, the Jenaama/Sorogama dialect of the Bozo language is usually referred to as Sorko. It is spoken in the Nigerian states of Niger, Kebbi, and Kwara (Lake Kainji). Writing system.

text: Bozo, Jenaama. Language code (ISO 639-3): bze. Population: 197,000 in Mali (2003 SIL), increasing. Region: Administrative circles of Djenné, Mopti, Youwarou, Tenenkou and Bandiagara.

title: Bozo language
text: Nigeria hosts one of the larger Bozo diaspora groups, with around 23,000 speakers of the Jenaama variety concentrated in Kebbi, Niger, and Kwara states, especially among fishermen around Lake Kainji.

title: Jenaama Bozo – TIPs
text: Tiéyaxo Bozo / Jenaama Bozo: “Salvation/Rescue (religious) feast” (source: Marko Hakkola). Sabaot: Saakweetaab Keeytaayeet — “Festival of Passing-by” (source: Iver Larsen). Language spoken in India and Bangladesh: “Festival of avoidance”.

title: Jenaama Bozo / Djenaama Bozo / Sorogaama Bozo
text: Other comments: Jenaama Bozo or Djenaama Bozo or Sorogaama Bozo is spoken by approximately 200,000 speakers in Mopti region: Djenné and Mopti circles on Niger river, Tenenkou and Youwarou circles; Ségou region: Niger river, upstream from Mopti, Mali as well as Nigeria.

title: The Verb in Bozo Jenaama.doc
text: Within Niger-Congo, Bozo is in the Northwestern branch of the Mande language family (Kastenholz 1996:70).Jenaama is spoken in the interior Delta of the Niger River in Mali, West Africa. Its southern border is around San, roughly 350 km northeast of the capital Bamako.
